document_text: We present a novel application of contrastive learning to scientific paper retrieval. Our method, ScholarCLIP, fine-tunes a SciBERT encoder using triplet loss on a curated dataset of 12,000 paired papers. Compared to a TF-IDF baseline and a vanilla SciBERT zero-shot embedding, ScholarCLIP achieves mean reciprocal rank of 0.74 (vs 0.41 baseline, 0.58 zero-shot). Ablations show contrastive triplet sampling contributes 0.12 MRR; domain-specific pretraining contributes 0.04. Authors are affiliated with University of Chicago. Funded by NSF grant CCF-2401234. The paper is released under CC-BY 4.0.

structured_abstract.problem: Scientific paper retrieval is weakly served by general-purpose embeddings and lexical baselines.
structured_abstract.approach: Fine-tune SciBERT with triplet contrastive loss on 12k paired papers.
structured_abstract.findings: MRR 0.74 vs 0.41 TF-IDF baseline and 0.58 zero-shot SciBERT.
structured_abstract.limitations: Single domain (CS); requires curated triplet pairs.

label.novelty_claim: First application of contrastive triplet learning fine-tuned on a curated paired-papers dataset for scientific paper retrieval (ScholarCLIP), with ablation isolating contrastive sampling as the dominant contributor (+0.12 MRR).
A new method for paper retrieval.
